title: Pappy
imageAlt: Portrait of Pappy, a druid-barbarian and plainspoken protector
dek: A simple, good man placed inside conflicts where goodness does not guarantee safety or clear information.

body:
Pappy is remembered through plainspoken care, hot springs, and a fundamentally good disposition. That simplicity does not keep him outside the setting’s hardest moral problems.

Support behind the Knights’ Pristinia shop

In the shop history, Farkur credits Pappy with paying for the location used by Ryvyting Creations and discusses a deed arrangement framed around ten pieces of jerky. This makes Pappy a substantial material supporter of shared Ale-Chemy Knights activity, beyond his social ties.

These are Farkur’s property accounts; Ryvyt is the shop’s established owner and operator. Financial support does not establish Pappy’s sole control of the business or formal faction membership.

The Rift ambush

Pappy joins the Rift alongside characters with very different moral commitments and is ambushed. Adelia senses betrayal and Gates him out. The event later becomes a dispute about what Adelia could know in character and what deeper mechanics permitted.

Character and governance

The physical rescue, the characters’ knowledge, the mechanical ruling, and the later out-of-character dispute are separate layers of evidence. The Codex preserves Pappy’s danger and escape without using sympathy to settle the governance question.

Contemporary reputation · 12 December 2024 and 2 September 2025

Ada remembers Pappy as a welcoming elder, informal historian, host, mentor, and guardian whose authority does not depend on claiming leadership. In public memory, the Gate and Hotsprings make welcome itself part of Prima’s defense against despair. Read the chronicler’s evidence boundary.

The Gate and the Hotsprings

Pappy’s two most characteristic places complete one another: the Gate is arrival, duty, watchfulness, and defense; Pappy’s Hotsprings are welcome, rest, recovery, and belonging. He protects people when they arrive and gives them somewhere to recover once they are safe.

Coffee at the threshold

When the robed newcomer Pin introduces himself, Pappy offers coffee, prepares it with Herb’s whiskey and shares sugar. Pin says he comes from Midgard to help allies he calls Rahu against Death. Eldin questions how those people relate to Fenumion’s Rahu, then offers directions to the Common Man. The hospitality is witnessed; Pin’s report does not settle the identity or politics of every Rahu group.

Caretaker of the Last Grove

At the Last Grove, Pappy communes with Physisia, accepts exhaustion and offers spell slots and vitality to sustain her. He recognises the invisible Druidic inscription and its warning against limitless union. When the spores spread, he returns to hear her report that a fiend has entered the forest.

30 September · carrying Papirak

Pappy carries Papirak’s casket and speaks to him through tears. He calls himself the last of their generation and remembers a partnership of different strengths. Those words establish his experience of loss, without independently resolving the ancient chronology he recounts.

At the Hearth he sets out jerky for others before sitting alone. Bitoshi, Jiangshi and Adelia’s projection remain near while giving him space. The same person who welcomes arrivals now needs company that does not demand he stop grieving. Read the funeral’s civic consequences.

Scene sources: 1, 2, 3, 4.

A small beginning after the blight

Pappy tries to help the sick Murr and stays with Sildithas and Coralyn to confront the blight. The fiend falls, but its threats about Alfred’s soul are not independently verified. Pappy recognizes a new mushroom as an ordinary kind, distinct from the one on his own head, and encourages its growth.

His role is patient as well as violent: a single bloom does not heal a forest immediately. The narrator explicitly gives recovery time rather than granting an instant reset.

Scene references: 1, 2, 3, 4, 5.

Clarity beside the Chains

During the later inspection, Pappy feels clarity where magic is suppressed. He recalls Voraketh as a druidic center known through accounts of natural wonders and people and beasts living together. The narrator explicitly says he had not personally visited that earlier place.

His further recollection is a rumor about an unnamed woman who always wanted more. The name is fuzzy, the chronology incomplete and the Maw’s making beyond the explanation supplied. His grief for the losses is witnessed without turning the rumor into a solved identity or origin.

Scene references: 1, 2, 3, 4.

brief.basis: Existing public dossier, explicit status facts and named timeline participants. Selected events are a reading guide, not a complete list or a ranking of importance.

profile.personality: Pappy is plainspoken, warm, and fundamentally inclined to protect. His simplicity is not foolishness; it is a refusal to let complicated politics obscure whether a person in front of him needs help.
profile.achievements: He survives the Rift ambush when Adelia senses betrayal and Gates him out, then continues into later disputes and the physical dangers of Voraketh. Near the Maw, antimagic makes bodily resilience more important than elaborate powers, allowing Pappy’s direct strength to become exactly the kind of protection the company needs. The McKalister mansion branch ends with a misunderstanding resolved over the family’s boxed collectible haul. Explored the Alpine Forest with Iridos and helped Dale think through drainage near the walls. Identifies new ordinary growth after the fiend’s fall, then recalls limited accounts of an earlier Voraketh.
profile.relationships: Adelia’s rescue is central, though the later governance dispute requires a strict boundary between what characters knew and what players or systems later argued. St. Anky carries Physisia’s message through Pappy in the Voraketh record, while the wider Ale-Chemy network treats him as a close contributor without proving formal membership.
